paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this room, friend. Jesus knows exactly what is coming, and He doesn't dodge it. He says the Son of Man will go "just as it is written about Him" (Matthew 26:24). He sits down at the table with the one who will betray Him and still passes the bread.

Then He takes the cup and says, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins" (Matthew 26:28). That is the heart of the whole night, baker. Forgiveness doesn't come from how well we hold up, and this passage proves it. Every one of those twelve is about to fall, and the cup is still for "all of you" (Matthew 26:27).

And then there's Peter. Bold Peter, promising with the whole room watching that he will never deny Jesus (Matthew 26:33-35). I've made promises like that, LOUD ones, with a timer already beeping. But look at how Jesus talks about the fall: He says it plainly, and in the same breath He promises, "after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee" (Matthew 26:32). So when you stumble, friend, don't run from Him. He already planned to go ahead of you, and the story isn't over.
